gaps.sentence: 'I'll call you later,' he promised. He promised that he ___ call me later.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll see you tomorrow,' he said. He said he would see me ___.
gaps.explanation: Time expressions shift: tomorrow becomes the next day / the following day.

gaps.sentence: 'Would you like to stay for dinner?' they asked. They ___ me to stay for dinner.
gaps.explanation: Offers of this kind are reported as invited somebody to do something.

gaps.sentence: "I saw him yesterday." — He said he ___ him the day before.
gaps.explanation: Backshift one step: saw → had seen; yesterday → the day before.

gaps.sentence: "We are leaving now." — They said they ___ then.
'The shop closes at six,' she reminded me. She reminded me that the shop ___ at six.
gaps.explanation: Even habitual present simple backshifts after a past reporting verb: closes → closed.

gaps.sentence: 'Why hasn't she replied?' he wondered. He wondered why she ___ replied.
gaps.explanation: hasn't replied → hadn't replied: statement order and past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'Where will you be staying?' they asked. They asked where ___ be staying.
gaps.hint: future continuous backshift in a question
gaps.explanation: will you be staying → I would be staying: statement order, would for will.
